markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (69%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert
Image flagged by the reliability check [F6], second model disagrees, and invasive stays in the conformal set.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 69%, Invasive 24% | InSitu leads, invasive plausible |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.77 / OOD percentile 1.00 | Flagged; input suspect |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Models pick different classes |
| Similar cases | 1 of 5 match InSitu | Weak neighbor support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 10) · ↑ invasive · Below-typical score; concept model leans away from invasive [F2] · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 0, 1, 8) · ↓ invasive · Above-typical score; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F4] · Weak
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 11) · ↑ invasive · Below-typical score; slight lean away from invasive · Validated
- **Tumor necrosis** (region 6) · ↑ invasive · Above-typical score; spot check 3/20, disregard · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions lowers the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion difference 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0: not shown to reflect the classifier. Necrosis (3/20) is unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Resampling degradation (severity 3) distorted the image and therefore every score.
- Invasive carcinoma, at 24%, remains inside the conformal set.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 6, 11**: Highest heatmap contribution toward invasive; look for invasive growth.
2. **Regions 0, 1, 8**: Confirm atypical cells remain confined within ducts.
3. **Region 10**: Strongest tile for infiltrating stroma; confirm whether stroma is infiltrated.
